questions.q: $\mathrm{R}=65 \pm 1 \Omega \mathrm{L}, \mathrm{l}=5 \pm 0.1 \mathrm{~mm}$ and $\mathrm{d}=10 \pm 0.5 \mathrm{~mm}$. Find error in calculation of resistivity.
questions.solution:
Given that, $\mathrm{R}=65 \Omega, \Delta \mathrm{R}=1 \Omega, \mathrm{l}=5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$, $\Delta \mathrm{l}=0.1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}, \mathrm{~d}=10 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}, \Delta \mathrm{d}=0.5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}\because$ Resistivity, $\rho=\frac{R A}{l}$
or $\quad \rho=\frac{\mathrm{R} \pi(\mathrm{d} / 2)^2}{\mathrm{l}}=\frac{\pi \mathrm{Rd}^2}{4 \mathrm{l}}\begin{array}{ll}\therefore & \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}}+2 \frac{\Delta \mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}}{\mathrm{l}} \\ \therefore & \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=\frac{1}{65}+2\left(\frac{0.5 \times 10^{-3}}{10 \times 10^{-3}}\right)+\frac{0.1 \times 10^{-3}}{5 \times 10^{-3}}\end{array}$
or $\quad \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=0.0153+0.1+0.02$
or $\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \approx 0.1353$
So, error in calculation of resistivity is
$13.5 \% \approx 13 \%$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Velocity is given by $v=4 t(1-2 t)$, then find time at which velocity is maximum
questions.solution:
To find value of time at which velocity is maximum, taking differentiation of v with respect to time
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}=0$
Here, $v=4 t(l-2 t)\begin{array}{lc} & \mathrm{v}=4 \mathrm{t}-8 \mathrm{t}^2 \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dt}}\left(4 \mathrm{t}-8 \mathrm{t}^2\right)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 4-16 \mathrm{t}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \mathrm{t}=\frac{1}{4} \mathrm{~s}=0.25 \mathrm{~s}\end{array}$
Again taking differentiation,
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{d}^2 v}{\mathrm{dt}^2}=-16 \lt 0$
So, at $\mathrm{t}=0.25 \mathrm{~s}$ velocity is maximum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed $u$ from a height h above the ground. The time taken by the ball to hit the ground is
questions.solution:
Time taken to reach the highest point from the height h is obtained from equation, $\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{u}-\mathrm{gt}\therefore \quad 0=\mathrm{u}-\mathrm{gt}$ or $\mathrm{t}=\frac{\mathrm{u}}{\mathrm{g}}$
Height attained above h is obtained from
$\mathrm{v}^2-\mathrm{u}^2=2(-\mathrm{g}) \mathrm{h}_1$
or $\quad 0-\mathrm{u}^2=2(-\mathrm{g}) \mathrm{h}_1$ or $\mathrm{h}_1=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2}{2 \mathrm{~g}}$
Total height, $\mathrm{h}_2=\left[\mathrm{h}_1+\mathrm{h}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2}{2 \mathrm{~g}}+\mathrm{h}\right]$
Time taken to hit the ground is obtained from,
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{h}_2 & =\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{at}^2 \\ \frac{\mathrm{u}^2}{2 \mathrm{~g}}+\mathrm{h} & =0+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{gt}^2\end{aligned}\therefore$ Total time taken, $\mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\frac{\left(\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~h}\right)}{\mathrm{g}^2}}$

questions.q: A runner starts from O and goes to O following path OQRO in lhr. What is net displacement and average speed?

So, net displacement is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the range of a projectile thrown with velocity $98 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ with angle $30^{\circ}$ from horizontal ?
questions.solution: Given, $\mathrm{U}=98 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, \theta=30^{\circ}\because$ Range of a projectile, $\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{U}^2 \sin (2 \theta)}{\mathrm{g}}=\frac{98 \times 98 \times \sin 60^{\circ}}{9.8}=490 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 0.5 kg for 0.25 s starting from rest. What is its momentum now?
questions.solution: Given, $\mathrm{F}=10 \mathrm{~N}, \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{i}}=0, \mathrm{~m}=0.5 \mathrm{~kg}, \Delta \mathrm{t}=0.25 \mathrm{~s}\because$ Change in momentum, $\Delta \mathrm{p}=\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{f}}\begin{aligned} \because & \Delta \mathrm{p} & =\mathrm{F} \cdot \Delta \mathrm{t} \\ & & \mathrm{F} \cdot \Delta \mathrm{t}=\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{i}}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \text { or } & & 10 \times 0.25 & =\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{f}}-0.5 \times 0 \\ \text { or } & & \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{f}} & =2.5 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball of 0.5 kg collided with wall at $30^{\circ}$ and bounced back elastically. The speed of ball was $12 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The contact remained for 1 s . What is the force applied by wall on ball?
questions.solution: Given, $\mathrm{m}=0.5 \mathrm{~kg}, \mathrm{v}=12 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, \Delta \mathrm{t}=1 \mathrm{~s}, \theta=30^{\circ}$ Force applied by wall on ball, $\mathrm{F}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{p}}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}$ or $\quad \mathrm{F}=\frac{\left(\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{f}}\right)_{\mathrm{H}}-\left(\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)_{\mathrm{H}}}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}$ In this elastic collision, final and initial velocity will be same but direction will changed. $\therefore$ Horizontal component, $\left(\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{f}}\right)_{\mathrm{H}}=\mathrm{mv} \cos \theta$ and $\left(\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)_{\mathrm{H}}=-\mathrm{mv} \cos \theta\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{F}=\frac{\mathrm{mv} \cos \theta-(-\mathrm{mV} \cos \theta)}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{mV} \cos \theta}{\Delta \mathrm{t}} \\ & =\frac{2 \times 0.5 \times 12 \times \cos 30^{\circ}}{1}=6 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~N} \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 1000 N force is required to lift a hook and 10000 N force is requires to lift a load slowly. Find power required to lift hook with load with speed $\mathrm{v}=0.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
questions.solution:
$\because$ Net force required to lift a hook and load,
$\mathrm{F}_{\text {net }}=1000+10000=11000 \mathrm{~N}\because$ Power required to lift hook, $\mathrm{P}=\frac{\mathrm{W}}{\mathrm{t}}\begin{aligned} \because \quad \mathrm{W} & =\mathrm{F}_{\text {net }} \mathrm{d} \\ \mathrm{P} \times \mathrm{t} & =\mathrm{F}_{\text {net }} \mathrm{d} \\ \mathrm{P} & =\frac{\mathrm{F}_{\text {net }} \mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{F}_{\text {net }}\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{t}}\right)=\mathrm{F}_{\text {net }} \mathrm{V} \quad\left[\text { Here, } \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{t}}\right]\end{aligned}$
or $\mathrm{P}=11000 \times 0.5=5500 \mathrm{~W}=5.5 \mathrm{~kW}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Kinetic energy of a particle is increased by 4 times. What will be the relation between initial and final momentum?
questions.solution:
$\because$ Relation between kinetic energy and momentum is $\mathrm{p}_1=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mk}_1}\because$ Kinetic energy is increased by 4 times
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{k}_2=4 \mathrm{k}_1$
Hence, $\mathrm{p}_2=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mk}_2}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~m}\left(4 \mathrm{k}_1\right)}=2 \sqrt{2 \mathrm{mk}_1}$
or $\quad \mathrm{p}_2=2 \mathrm{p}_1$

questions.q: A machine gun fires 360 bullets per minute, with a velocity of $600 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. If the power of the gun is 5.4 kW , then mass of each bullet is
questions.solution:
Here, $\mathrm{n}=\frac{360}{60}=6$ bullets s ${ }^{-1}$
Velocity, $\mathrm{v}=600 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}, \mathrm{~m}=$ ?
Power of gun = Power of bullets
$5.4 \times 10^3=\frac{1}{2}(\mathrm{~nm}) \mathrm{v}^22 \times 5400=6 \times \mathrm{m}(600)^2$
or $\quad \begin{aligned} \mathrm{m} & =\frac{2 \times 5400}{6 \times 600 \times 600} \mathrm{~kg} \\ & =\frac{1}{200} \mathrm{~kg}=\frac{1000}{200} \mathrm{~g}=5 \mathrm{~g}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Find ratio of radius of gyration of a disk and ring of same radii at their tangential axis in plane.
questions.solution:
For disk, moment of inertia about the diameter, $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{4}$ and moment of inertia about the tangential axis
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}_{\text {disc }}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}+\mathrm{mr}^2 \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\text {disc }}=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{4}+\mathrm{mr}^2 \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\text {disc }}=\frac{5 \mathrm{mr}^2}{4}\end{aligned}$
Let the radius of gyration of disc is $\mathrm{k}_{\text {disc }}$.
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_{\text {disc }} & =\mathrm{mk}_{\text {disc }}^2 \\ \frac{5 \mathrm{mr}^2}{4} & =\mathrm{mk}_{\text {disc }}^2 \\ \mathrm{k}_{\text {disc }}^2 & =\sqrt{\frac{5}{4} \mathrm{r}}\end{aligned}$
For ring, moment of inertia about the diameter
$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{a}}^{\prime}=\mathrm{mr}^2 / 2$
and moment of inertia about the tangential axis
$\mathrm{I}_{\text {ring }}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{a}}^{\prime}+\mathrm{mr}^2=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{2}+\mathrm{mr}^2=\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{mr}^2$
Let the radius of gyration of ring $\mathrm{k}_{\text {ring }}$.
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_{\text {ring }} & =\mathrm{mk}^2 \text { ring } \\ \frac{3}{2} \mathrm{mr}^2 & =\mathrm{mk}^2 \text { ring } \\ \mathrm{k}_{\text {ring }} & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \mathrm{r} \\ \frac{\mathrm{k}_{\text {disc }}}{\mathrm{k}_{\text {ring }}} & =\frac{\sqrt{\frac{5}{4} \mathrm{r}}}{\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \mathrm{r}}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{6}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform rod of mass m and length $l_0$ is pivoted at one end and is hanging in the vertical direction. The period of small angular oscillations of the rod is
questions.solution:
Here, the rod is oscillating about an end point $O$. Hence, moment of inertia of rod about the point of oscillating is
$\mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{~m} l_0^2$
Moreover, length $l$ of the pendulum = distance from the oscillation axis to centre of mass of rod
$=l_0 / 2\therefore$ Time period of oscillation,
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{I}}{\mathrm{mg} l}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\frac{\mathrm{l}}{3} \mathrm{~m} l_0^2}{m g\left(\frac{l_0}{2}\right)}} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{2 l_0}{3 \mathrm{~g}}} \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A disc of moment of inertia $2 \mathrm{~kg}-\mathrm{m}^2$ revolving with $8 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ is placed on another disc of moment of inertia $4 \mathrm{~kg}-\mathrm{m}^2$ revolving $4 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$. What is the angular frequency of composite disc?
questions.solution:
Given that, moment of inertia of discs,
$\mathrm{I}_1=2 \mathrm{~kg}-\mathrm{m}^2, \mathrm{I}_2=4 \mathrm{~kg}-\mathrm{m}^2$
Angular velocity of discs, $\omega_1=8 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$, $\omega_2=4 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
From angular momentum conservation principle,
$\mathrm{I}_1 \omega_1+\mathrm{I}_2 \omega_2=\left(\mathrm{I}_1+\mathrm{I}_2\right) \omega$
or $\quad 2 \times 8+4 \times 4=(2+4) \omega$
or $\quad \omega=\frac{16+16}{6}=\frac{32}{6}=\frac{16}{3} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At what distance (in metre) from the centre of the Moon, the intensity of gravitational field will be zero? (Take, mass of Earth and Moon as $5.98 \times 10^{24} \mathrm{~kg}$ and $7.35 \times 10^{22} \mathrm{~kg}$ respectively and the distance between Moon and Earth is $3.85 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m}$.)
questions.solution:
Let X be the distance of the point from the centre of earth where gravitational intensity is zero. Therefore,
$\frac{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}}}{\mathrm{x}^2}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{m}}}{\left(3.85 \times 10^8-\mathrm{x}\right)^2}$
or $\frac{\mathrm{x}}{3.85 \times 10^8-\mathrm{x}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{e}}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{m}}}}=\sqrt{\frac{5.98 \times 10^{24}}{7.35 \times 10^{22}}} \cong 9$
or $\quad \frac{x}{9}+x=3.85 \times 10^8$
or $\quad \mathrm{x}=9 \times 3.85 \times 10^8 / 10=3.46 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m}$
Distance from Moon $=3.85 \times 10^8-3.46 \times 10^8=3.9 \times 10^7 \mathrm{~m} \cong 3.85 \times 10^7 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: R is the radius of Earth and $\omega$ is its angular velocity and $g_p$ is the value of $g$ at the poles. The effective value of $g$ at a latitude $\lambda=60^{\circ}$.
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity at a latitude $\lambda$ is
$\mathrm{g}^{\prime}=\mathrm{g}-\mathrm{R} \omega^2 \cos ^2 \lambda$
At the poles, $\lambda=90^{\circ}\therefore \quad \mathrm{g}^{\prime}=\mathrm{g}=\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{p}}$
For $\quad \lambda=60^{\circ}$,
$\mathrm{g}^{\prime}=\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{p}}-\mathrm{R} \omega^2 \cos ^2 \lambda$
or $\quad g^{\prime}=g_p-R \omega^2 \cos ^2 60^{\circ}=g_p-R \omega^2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2=g_p-\frac{1}{4} R \omega^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If compressibility of material is $4 \times 10^{-5}$ per atm, pressure is 100 atm and volume is $100 \mathrm{~cm}^3$, then find $\Delta \mathrm{V}=$ ?
questions.solution:
$\because$ Compressibility
$|\beta|=\frac{1}{\mid \text { Bulk modulus of elasticits } \mid}|\beta|=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{pV}}{\Delta \mathrm{V}}$
or $\quad \beta=\frac{l}{\left(\frac{\Delta \mathrm{pV}}{\Delta \mathrm{V}}\right)}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{\Delta \mathrm{pV}}\begin{aligned} \therefore \Delta \mathrm{V}=\beta(\Delta \mathrm{p} . \mathrm{V}) & =4 \times 10^{-5}\left(100 \times 100 \times 10^{-6}\right) \\ & =0.4 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~m}^3=0.4 \mathrm{~cm}^3\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rain drop of radius 0.3 mm has a terminal velocity in air $1 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. The viscosity of air is $18 \times 10^{-5}$ poise. Find the viscous force on the rain drops.
questions.solution:
Here, $\mathrm{r}=0.3 \mathrm{~mm}=0.3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}, \mathrm{v}=1 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}\eta=18 \times 10^{-5}$ poise $=18 \times 10^{-6}$ decapoise
Viscous force, $\mathrm{F}=6 \pi \eta \mathrm{rv}\begin{aligned} & =6 \times \frac{22}{7} \times\left(18 \times 10^{-6}\right) \times\left(0.3 \times 10^{-3}\right) \times 1 \\ & =1.018 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Find density of ethyl alcohol
questions.solution:
Pressure at left hand of U-tube,
$p_1=p_0+\rho_1 g h_1=p_0+\rho_1 g\left(10 \times 10^{-2}\right)$
or $\quad \mathrm{p}_1=\mathrm{p}_0+\rho_1$
Pressure at right hand of u-tube,
$\begin{aligned} & p_2=p_0+\rho_2 g h_2=p_0+\rho_2 g\left(12 \times 10^{-2}\right) \\ & \text { or } \quad \mathrm{p}_2=\mathrm{p}_0+1.2 \rho_2 \\ & \end{aligned}$
The mercury column in both arms of $U$-tube are at same level, therefore pressure in both arms will be same.
or $\quad \mathrm{p}_1=\mathrm{p}_2\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{p}_0+\rho_1=\mathrm{p}_0+1.2 \rho_2\therefore$ Density of ethyl alcohol,
$\rho_2=\frac{\rho_1}{1.2}=\frac{1000}{1.2}=833.3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3=0.83 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{cm}^3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Water flows through a horizontal pipe of variable cross-section at the rate of $20 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{~min}^{-1}$. What will be the velocity of water at a point where diameter is 4 cm ?
questions.solution:
Volume of the water flowing per second,
$\mathrm{V}=20 \mathrm{Lmin}^{-1}=\frac{20 \times 1000}{60 \times(100)^3} \mathrm{~m}^3 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}=\frac{1}{3} \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^3 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$
Radius of the pipe,
$\mathrm{r}=\frac{4}{2}=2 \mathrm{~cm}=0.02 \mathrm{~m}$
Area of cross-section,
$\mathrm{r}=\pi \mathrm{r}^2=\frac{22}{7} \times(0.02)^2 \mathrm{~m}^2$
Let $v$ be the velocity of the flow of water at the given point. Clearly, $\mathrm{V}=\mathrm{Av}$
or $\quad \frac{1}{3} \times 10^{-3}=\frac{22}{7} \times(0.02)^2 \times v$
or $\quad \mathrm{v}=\frac{7 \times 10^{-3}}{3 \times 22 \times(0.02)^2}=0.2639 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid floats with $1 / 4$ th of its volume above the surface of water, the density of the solid is
questions.solution:
Let V and $\rho$ be volume and density of solid respectively and $\rho^{\prime}$ be the density of water i.e., $\mathrm{p}^{\prime}=10^3 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$
Weight of body $=\mathrm{V} \rho g$
Volume of solid body outside water $=\mathrm{V} / 4\therefore$ Volume of solid body inside water
$=\mathrm{V}-\mathrm{V} / 4=3 \mathrm{~V} / 4$
Weight of water displaced by solid
$=\frac{3 \mathrm{~V}}{4} \times 10^3 \times \mathrm{g}$
As solid body is floating, then
Weight of body $=$ Weight of water displaced by it
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{V} \rho g & =\frac{3 \mathrm{~V}}{4} \times 10^3 \mathrm{~g} \\ \rho & =\frac{3}{4} \times 1000=750 \mathrm{kgm}^{-3}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The work done in blowing a soap bubble of surface tension $0.06 \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$ from 2 cm radius to 5 cm radius is
questions.solution:
Here, $S=0.06 \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$,
$\mathrm{r}_1=2 \mathrm{~cm}=0.02 \mathrm{~m}, \mathrm{r}_2=5 \mathrm{~cm}=0.05 \mathrm{~m}$
Since, bubble has two surfaces, initial surface area of the bubble
$\begin{aligned} & =2 \times 4 \pi r_1^2=2 \times 4 \pi(0.02)^2 \\ & =32 \pi \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2\end{aligned}$
Final surface area of the bubble
$\begin{aligned} & =2 \times 4 \pi r_2^2=2 \times 4 \pi(0.05)^2 \\ & =200 \pi \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2\end{aligned}$
Final surface area of the bubble
$\begin{aligned} & =2 \times 4 \pi \mathrm{r}_2^2=2 \times 4 \pi(0.05)^2 \\ & =200 \pi \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2\end{aligned}$
Increase in surface area
$\begin{aligned} & =200 \pi \times 10^{-4}-32 \pi \times 10^{-4} \\ & =168 \pi \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2\end{aligned}\therefore$ Work done $=\mathrm{S} \times$ Increase in surface area
$=0.06 \times 168 \pi \times 10^{-4}=0.003168 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At what speed will the velocity of a stream of water be equal to 20 cm of mercury column? (Taking, $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ )
questions.solution:
Here, velocity head $=20 \mathrm{~cm}$ of Hg
$=20 \times 13.6 \mathrm{~cm}$ of water.
As, velocity head $=\frac{v^2}{2 \mathrm{~g}}\therefore \quad 20 \times 13.6=\frac{\mathrm{v}^2}{2 \times 1000}\begin{aligned} \mathrm{v} & =\sqrt{20 \times 13.6 \times 2 \times 1000} \\ & =737.56 \mathrm{cms}^{-1} \\ & =7.3756 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: How much should the temperature of a brass rod be increased so as to increase its length by $1 \%$ ? (Given, $\alpha$ for brass is $0.00002^{\circ} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$ ).
questions.solution:
Here, $\Delta \mathrm{T}=$ ?, $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{L}}{\mathrm{L}}=\frac{1}{100}\alpha=0.00002^{\circ} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$
As $\Delta \mathrm{L}=\alpha \mathrm{L} \Delta \mathrm{T}\therefore \quad \alpha \Delta \mathrm{T}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{L}}{\mathrm{L}}$
or $\Delta \mathrm{T}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{L}}{\mathrm{L} \alpha}=\frac{1}{100 \times 0.00002}\Delta \mathrm{T}=\frac{10^5}{2 \times 10^2}=500^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The coefficient of volume expansion of glycerine is $49 \times 10^{-50} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$. What is the fractional change in density for a $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ rise in temperature?
questions.solution:
Here, $\gamma=49 \times 19^{-5}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}^{-1}\begin{aligned} \Delta \mathrm{T} & =30^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \mathrm{V}^{\prime} & =\mathrm{V}+\Delta \mathrm{V}=\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{l}+\gamma \Delta \mathrm{T})\end{aligned}\therefore \quad \mathrm{V}^{\prime}=\mathrm{V}\left(1+49 \times 10^{-5} \times 30\right)=1.0147 \mathrm{~V}\because \quad \rho=\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{V}}$ and $\rho^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{V}^{\prime}}=\frac{\mathrm{m}}{0.0147}=0.9855 \rho$
Hence, fractional change in density
$=\frac{\rho-\rho^{\prime}}{\rho}=\frac{\rho-0.9855 \rho}{\rho}=0.0145$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a machine perform 4000 J output work and 1000 J is inside loss due to friction, then the find efficiency?
questions.solution: $\because$ Efficiency $=\frac{\text { output work }}{\text { input work }} \times 100=\frac{\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{o}}}{\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{i}}} \times 100\begin{aligned} & \because \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{o}}=4000 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{i}}=4000+1000=5000 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \therefore \text { Efficiency }=\frac{4000}{5000} \times 100=80 \%\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The efficiency of an ideal gas with adiabatic exponent $\gamma$ for the shown cyclic process would be
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{As}, \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{BC}}=\mathrm{p} \Delta \mathrm{V}=\mathrm{nR} \Delta \mathrm{T}=-\mathrm{nR}\left(2 \mathrm{~T}_0-\mathrm{T}_0\right)=\mathrm{nRT}_0\begin{aligned} & \text { and } \quad \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{CA}}=+2 \mathrm{nRT}_0 \ln 2 \\ & \text { Work done }=\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{CA}}+\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{BC}} \\ & =2 \mathrm{nRT}_0 \ln 2-\mathrm{nRT}_0 \\ & =\operatorname{nRT}_0(2 \ln 2-1) \\ & \end{aligned}$
Also, input heat, $\Delta \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{BC}}=\mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{p}} \Delta \mathrm{T}=\frac{\mathrm{nR} \gamma \mathrm{T}_0}{\gamma-1}$
Efficiency $=\frac{\text { Work }}{\text { Input heat }}=\frac{(2 \ln 2-1)}{\gamma /(\gamma-1)}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the efficiency of an engine is $50 \%$ and its work output is 500 J , then find input.
questions.solution:
$\because$ Efficiency, $\eta=\frac{\text { Workdone }}{\text { Heat input }} \times 100$
or $\frac{\eta}{100}=\frac{\text { Work done }}{\text { Heat input }}=\frac{500}{\text { Heat input }}$
Heat input $=\frac{500 \times 100}{50}=1000 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.q: The efficiency of a heat engine is $1 / 6$. Its efficiency double when the temperature of sink decrease by $62^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, its efficiency doubles. Then, what is the temperature of source?
questions.solution:
$\because$ Efficiency of a heat engine,
$\eta=1-\frac{\mathrm{T}_2}{\mathrm{~T}_1}$
or $\quad \frac{1}{6}=1-\frac{\mathrm{T}_2}{\mathrm{~T}_1}\frac{\mathrm{T}_2}{\mathrm{~T}_1}=1-\frac{1}{6}=\frac{5}{6} \Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_2=\frac{5 \mathrm{~T}_1}{6}$  ...(i)
According to question, it's efficiency is doubled when temperature of sink decreased by $62^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.
$\therefore \quad 2 \eta=1-\frac{\mathrm{T}_2-62}{\mathrm{~T}_1}\Rightarrow \quad 2\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)=1-\frac{\left(\frac{5 T_1}{6}-62\right)}{T_1} \quad$ [From Eq. (i)]
$\begin{array}{rlrl}\Rightarrow & \frac{5 \mathrm{~T}_1}{6}-62 & =\mathrm{T}_1\left(1-\frac{2}{6}\right)=\frac{2 \mathrm{~T}_1}{3} \\ \text { or } & \frac{5 \mathrm{~T}_1}{6}-\frac{2 \mathrm{~T}_1}{3} & =62 \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{6}=62 \\ \text { or } & \mathrm{T}_1=372 \mathrm{~K}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A Carnot engine absorbs $6 \times 10^5 \mathrm{cal}$ at $227^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The work done per cycle by the engine, if its sink is maintained at $127^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is
questions.solution:
Here, $\mathrm{Q}_1=6 \times 10^5 \mathrm{cal}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}_1=227^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=227+273=500 \mathrm{~K} \\ & \mathrm{~T}_2=127^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=127+273=400 \mathrm{~K}\end{aligned}$
Work done/cycle, $\mathrm{W}=$ ?
As $\frac{\mathrm{Q}_2}{\mathrm{Q}_1}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_2}{\mathrm{~T}_1}$ or
$\mathrm{Q}_2=\frac{\mathrm{T}_2}{\mathrm{~T}_1} \times \mathrm{Q}_1=\frac{400}{500} \times 6 \times 10^5=4.8 \times 10^5 \mathrm{cal}\begin{aligned} \text { As, } & \mathrm{W}=\mathrm{Q}_1-\mathrm{Q}_2=6 \times 10^5-4.8 \times 10^5 \\ \mathrm{~W} & =1.2 \times 10^5 \mathrm{cal}=1.2 \times 10^5 \times 4.2 \mathrm{~J} \\ \mathrm{~W} & =5.04 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass of Hg is executing SHM which is given by $x=6.0 \cos \left(100 t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \mathrm{cm}$. What is the maximum kinetic energy?
questions.solution:
Here, $\mathrm{m}=1 \mathrm{~kg}$
The given equation of SHM is
$x=6.0 \cos \left(100 t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
Comparing it with equation of SHM,
$\begin{aligned} x & =A \cos (\omega t+\phi), \text { we have } \\ A & =6.0 \mathrm{~cm}=\frac{6}{100} \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$
and $\quad \omega=100 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
Maximum kinetic energy $=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}\left(\mathrm{v}_{\max }\right)^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}(\mathrm{~A} \omega)^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times\left[\frac{6}{100} \times 100\right]^2=18 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $Y=5 \sin \frac{\pi}{2}(100 t-2 x)$, what is time period?
questions.solution:
Given that,
$Y=5 \sin (50 \pi t-\pi x)$  ...(i)
Equation of displacement,
$Y=A \sin (\omega t-k x)$  ...(ii)
After comparing with Eqs. (i) and (ii),
$\omega=50 \pi\because$ Time period, $\mathrm{T}=\frac{2 \pi}{\omega}=\frac{2 \pi}{50 \pi}=0.04 \mathrm{~s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle doing SHM having amplitude 5 cm , mass 0.5 kg and angular frequency $5 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ is at 1 cm from mean position. Find potential energy and kinetic energy.
questions.solution:
Given, $\mathrm{m}=0.5 \mathrm{~kg} . \omega=5 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}, \mathrm{x}=10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}$,$\mathrm{A}=5 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}\because$ Potential energy, $\mathrm{U}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m} \omega^2 \mathrm{x}^2$
or $\quad \mathrm{U}=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times(5)^2 \times\left(10^{-2}\right)^2=\frac{25}{4} \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~J}=6.25 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~J}\because$ Kinetic energy, $\mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m} \omega^2\left(\mathrm{~A}^2-\mathrm{x}^2\right)$
or $\mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times(5)^2(25-1) \times 10^{-4}=150 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If speed of sound in air is $340 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and in water is $1480 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If frequency of sound is 1000 kHz, then find wavelength in water
questions.solution:
Given that, $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{w}}=1480 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, \mathrm{f}=1000 \mathrm{kHz}$
Speed, $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{w}}=\mathrm{f} \lambda\therefore \quad \lambda=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{w}}}{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{1480}{1000 \times 10^3}=1.480 \mathrm{~mm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A organ pipe open on both ends in the $\mathrm{n}^{\text {th }}$ harmonic is in resonance with a source of 1000 Hz . The length of pipe is 16.6 cm and speed of sound in air is $332 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. Find the value of $n$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A electron $\left(\mathrm{e}^{-}\right)$is accelerated by V volts experiences a force F , when it enters in a uniform magnetic field. What will the force experienced when it is accelerated by 2 V ?
questions.solution:
When $\mathrm{e}^{-}$is accelerated by V volts, then work done by $\mathrm{e}^{-}$is equals to kinetic energy of $\mathrm{e}^{-}$.
or $\quad \mathrm{qV}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2$
Then, the velocity of $\mathrm{e}^{-}$is $\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{qV}}{\mathrm{m}}}$ or $\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{k} \sqrt{\mathrm{V}}$. When $\mathrm{e}^{-}$accelerated by V volts, then $\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{k} \sqrt{\mathrm{V}}$.
Force experiences by $\mathrm{e}^{-}$in a uniform magnetic field, $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{qvB}$
or $\quad \mathrm{F}=\mathrm{qk} \sqrt{\mathrm{V} B}$  ...(i)
When e accelerated by 2 V volts, then $\mathrm{v}_1=\mathrm{k} \sqrt{2 \mathrm{~V}}$.
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{F}_1=\mathrm{qv}_1 \mathrm{~B}=\mathrm{qk} \sqrt{2 \mathrm{VB}}$
Hence, $\quad \mathrm{F}_1=\sqrt{2} \mathrm{~F} \quad$ [from Eq. (i)]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Electron revolving with speed v is producing magnetic field B at centre. Find relation between radius of path $B$ and $v$ ?
questions.solution:
$\because$ Magnetic field at center,

where, $I=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{t}}$
or $\quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\left(\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{v}}\right)}=\frac{\mathrm{ev}}{2 \pi \mathrm{r}}$
Hence, $B=\left(\frac{\mu_0}{2 \mathrm{r}}\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{ev}}{2 \pi \mathrm{r}}\right)=\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{ev}}{4 \pi \mathrm{r}^2}$
or $\quad B \propto \frac{V}{r^2}$

questions.q: A regular hexagone of side a. A wire of length 24 a is coiled on that hexagone. If current in hexagone is I, then find the magnetic moment.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A prism of crown glass with refracting angle of $5^{\circ}$ and mean refractive index $=1.51$ is combined with a flint glass prism of refractive index $=1.65$ to produce no deviation. Find the angle of flint glass.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The refractive index of glass is 1.5 . The speed of light in glass is
questions.solution:

Given, $v_1=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\begin{array}{rlrl} & & \frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1} & ={ }^1 \mu_2=1.5 \\ \Rightarrow & & v_2 & =\frac{v_1}{{ }^1 \mu_2}=\frac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \therefore & & v_2=\frac{3 \times 10^8}{3 / 2}=2 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An atomic power nuclear reactor can deliver 300 MW. The energy released due to fission of each nucleus of uranium atoms $\mathrm{U}^{238}$ is 170 MeV . The number of uranium atoms fissioned per hour will be
questions.solution:
Power $=\frac{\text { Energy }}{\text { Time }}=300 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~W}=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{s}$
Energy released due to fission
$\begin{gathered}=170 \mathrm{MeV}=170 \times 10^6 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \\ =27.2 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~J}\end{gathered}$
Number of atoms fissioned per second
$=\frac{3 \times 10^8}{27.2 \times 10^{-12}}=\frac{3 \times 10^{20}}{27.2}$
Number of atoms fissioned per hour
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{3 \times 10^{20} \times 3600}{27.2} \\ & =\frac{3 \times 36}{27.2} \times 10^{22}=4 \times 10^{22} \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the fusion reaction ${ }_1^2 \mathrm{H}+{ }_1^2 \mathrm{H} \longrightarrow{ }_2^3 \mathrm{He}+{ }_0^1 \mathrm{n}$, the masses of deuteron, helium and neutron expressed in amu are $2.015,3.017$ and 1.009 , respectively. If 1 kg of deuterium undergoes complete fusion, find the amount of total energy released. (1 amu $=931.5 \mathrm{MeV})$.
questions.solution:
$\Delta \mathrm{m}=2(2.015)-(3.017+1.009)=0.004 \mathrm{amu}\therefore$ Energy released $=(0.004 \times 931.5) \mathrm{MeV}=3.726 \mathrm{MeV}$
Energy released per deuteron
$=\frac{3.726}{2}=1.863 \mathrm{MeV}$
Number of deuterons in 1 kg
$=\frac{6.02 \times 10^{26}}{2}=3.01 \times 10^{26}\therefore$ Energy released per kg of deuterium fusion
$\begin{aligned} & =\left(3.01 \times 10^{26} \times 1.863\right) \\ & =5.6 \times 10^{26} \mathrm{MeV} \approx 9.0 \times 10^{13} \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound, containing only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen has a molecular weight of 44 . On complete oxidation, it is converted into a compound of molecular weight is 60 . The original compound is
questions.solution:

questions.q: Valence electrons in the element X are 3 and that in element Y is 6. Most probable compound formed from X and Y is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following pair behaves as strong and weak base hydride repectively $\mathrm{NH}_3, \mathrm{PH}_3, \mathrm{AsH}_3, \mathrm{SbH}_3, \mathrm{BiH}_3$
questions.solution:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the complex, $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$, the oxidation number of Cr is
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation number of Cr is x in the complex $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \mathrm{X}+4 \times(0)+2 \times(-1) & =+1 \\ x-2 & =+1 \\ x & =+3\end{aligned}$
Thus, the oxidation number of Cr is +3 .

Arrange the following polymers in increasing order of their intermolecular forces.
Nylon-6, 6, buna-S, polythene, neoprene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which type of drugs come under anti-microbial drugs?
questions.solution: Bacteria, virus, fungi and other pathogens are microorganisms. These may cause diseases in human beings and animals. An antimicrobial drug prevents the development or inhibit the pathogenic action of microorganisms such as bacteria (antibacterial drug), virus (antiviral drugs), fungi (antifungal drugs) or other parasite (antiparasite drugs selectively). Antibiotics, antiseptics and disinfectants are antimicrobial drugs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cell wall of fungi is composed of
questions.solution: The cell wall of fungi is composed of chitin. It is the second most abundant carbohydrate. It is a homopolymer of N -Acetyl Glucosamine (NAG) joined with $\beta$ 1-4 linkages. NAG is a modification of glucose molecule.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which motile-stage of protozoans is helpful in feeding?
questions.solution: Pseudopodium is helpful in the feeding of protozoans. It is a temporary cytoplasm-filled projection of a eukaryotic cell membrane. It can be used for motility or for ingesting nutrients or other particulate matter.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Shape of chloroplast of Ulothrix is
questions.solution: The chloroplast of Ulothrix is girdle-shaped containing one or more pyrenoids. The thallus of Ulothrix is filamentous, long, unbranched and multicellular. It is a freshwater alga growing on substratum like rocks, sand, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one is a parasitic alga?
questions.solution: Cephaleuros is a parasitic thalloid green alga. Its common name is red rust. This alga is parasitic on some important economic plants of the tropics and subtropics, e.g. tea, guava, mango, coffee, etc. It damages the area of algal growth on leaves or kills the new shoots or disfigure fruit.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Heterotrichous thallus is shown by which organism?
questions.solution: The heterotrichous thallus is shown by Ectocarpus. It is a filamentous marine brown alga which has both upright and prostrate regions. Such a growth is called heterotrichous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Palmella stage is present in
questions.solution: lamydomonas. In adverse conditions, the daughter protoplasts formed by division, do not develop neuromotor apparatus and become motile. However, the parent cell wall gelatinises and forms a matrix around the daughter protoplasts. All cells of palmella stage develop flagella and become motile. They escape from the gelatinous matrix on the arrival of favourable conditions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Eyespot is seen in
questions.solution: Eyespot is seen in Chlamydomonas. It is a microscopic, eukaryotic, unicellular, pyriform, biflagellate alga. The alga possesses a cup-shaped chloroplast with a red eyespot or stigma and a pyrenoid for storing starch.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the symmetry of medusa?
questions.solution: The medusa of Obelia shows radial symmetry. It is a free-swimming, umbrella-like sexual generation. It is formed by blastostyle. It brings about sexual reproduction and dispersal of species.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Caryopsis is present in
questions.solution: heat. It is a type of simple dry fruit. It is also called as grain. In such fruits the ovary wall and seed coat fuse making it difficult to separate the two.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Perianth is found in which family?
questions.solution: Perianth is found in Liliaceae family when there is no distinction of sepals and petals. The individual parts of the perianth are known as tepals, e.g. onion, lily, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Above diagram represents
questions.solution: The given figure is showing anaphase-I of meiosis. It begins when the two chromosomes of each bivalent separate and start moving towards opposite poles of the cell. Unlike the anaphase of mitosis, the sister chromatids remain attached at their centromeres and move together toward the poles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Above diagram represents
questions.solution: The given diagram represents metaphase-I of meiosis. This stage is more or less similar to metaphase stage of mitosis. The only difference is appearance of paired chromosomes at metaphasic plate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is common between a eukaryotic and prokaryotic flagella?
options: Both are extension of cell membrane
questions.solution: The common feature between eukaryotic and prokaryotic flagella is that both are used for locomotion. Prokaryotic flagellum is single stranded while eukaryotic flagellum is 11-stranded. Eukaryotic flagellum has two parts, basal body and shaft, while prokaryotic flagellum consists of three parts, basal body, hook and filament. Prokaryotic and eukaryotic flagellum are made up of flagellin and tubulin proteins, respectively.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which is incorrect with reference to chloroplast?
options: Occurs only in cells with aerobic respiration
questions.solution: Option (3) is incorrect about chloroplasts. They are spherical, ovoid or disc-shaped cell organelles. These are found in plants and algae. They are involved in photosynthesis due to the presence of chlorophyll in them. During photosynthesis, $\mathrm{O}_2$ is released. They are not associated with any type of respiration, i.e. aerobic and anaerobic and can be found in any type of cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the role of sterol in cell membrane?
questions.solution: The role of sterol in cell membrane is to provide stability. Steroles are steroids with $8-10$ carbon long aliphatic side chain at carbon 17 and at least one alcoholic hydroxyl. Cholesterol $\left(\mathrm{C}_{27} \mathrm{H}_{45} \mathrm{OH}\right)$ is a common sterol found in many animal cell membranes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a plant growth inhibitor?
questions.solution: IAA is a plant growth promoter while dormin, abscisic acid and ethylene are plant growth inhibitors. IAA (indole 3-Acetic Acid) is an auxin. It was discovered by Koge et al. (1934). Auxins are synthesised in shoot apices, leaf primordia and developing seeds from amino acid, tryptophan.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed in glycolysis?
questions.solution:
In glycolysis, 2 molecules of pyruvic acid are formed. It is the first step of degradation of glucose. The main purpose of glycolysis is the generation of energy in the form of ATP.
However, comparatively more ATPs are formed downstream of glycolysis through the complete oxidation of pyruvate.

RQ is slightly more than unity when organic acids are broken down as respiratory substrates under aerobic conditions, e.g. malic acid.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Molecular formula of chlorophyll-b is
questions.solution: The molecular formula of chlorophyll-b is $\mathrm{C}_{55} \mathrm{H}_{70} \mathrm{O}_6 \mathrm{~N}_4 \mathrm{Mg}$. It helps in photosynthesis by absorbing light energy. It is more soluble in polar solvents than chlorophyll-a because of its carbonyl group. It is of yellow colour and primarily absorbs blue light.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these is incorrect for $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants?
questions.solution: Among the given options, option (4) is incorrect about $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants. The mesophyll cells of $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants do not possess RuBisCO enzyme. $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants show Kranz anatomy. In these plants, the initial fixation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ occurs in mesophyll cells. The primary acceptor of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is Phosphoenol Pyruvate or PEP. It combines with $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in the presence of PEP carboxylase or PEPCase to form oxaloacetic acid or oxaloacetate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Conditions required for cyclic photophosphorylation are
questions.solution:
The conditions required for cyclic photophosphorylation are aerobic condition and optimum light intensity.
It is a process of photophosphorylation in which an electron expelled by the excited photocentre is returned. This electron passes through a series of electron carriers. Cyclic photophosphorylation is performed by photosystem-I only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pollenkitt is present in
questions.solution: ntomophily. It is a sticky covering on the surface of pollen grains. Its major function is to make the pollen to stick to the bugs. Thus, it helps in the pollination.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a derivative of cholesterol?
questions.solution: Among the given options, vitamin- B is not a derivative of cholesterol. It (cholesterol) is a type of lipid molecule. It is an essential structural component of all animal cell membranes. It also serves as a precursor for the biosynthesis of steroid hormones, bile salts and vitamin-D.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Non-essential amino acid is
questions.solution: Among the given options, arginine is a non-essential amino acid. Such amino acids can be made within the body and so are not essential to the human diet. Valine, histidine and lysine are essential amino acids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Proteins are needed in diet because
options: all amino acids are not available in body
proteins act as building blocks of our body
questions.solution: Proteins are polymers of amino acids. These are divided into two categories; essential and nonessential amino acids. Essential amino acids cannot be synthesised in the body and therefore must be included in the diet. Proteins are used as structural components of tissues as channels, transporters, regulatory molecules and enzymes. Proteins can also be utilised as energy sources. Normally, this is a secondary function and becomes important only when there is not enough carbohydrate and fat in the body, e.g. during fasting.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Omega 3 fatty acid is present in
questions.solution: x seed oil. These are Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids (PUFAs). They are important for normal metabolism. Mammals are unable to synthesise omega 3 fatty acids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which is the 21 st amino acid?
questions.solution: Selenocysteine ( Sec ) is the 21 st amino acid in the genetic code. This amino acid contains selenium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Histamine is secreted by
questions.solution: ast cells. It is an organic nitrogenous compound involved in local immune responses. It is responsible for inflammatory responses. It increases the permeability of the capillaries to white blood cells and some proteins to allow them to engage pathogens in the infected tissues.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Function of hypothalamus is
questions.solution: The functions of hypothalamus include thermoregulation, water balance and control of hormone functions. It is located below the thalamus and is a part of limbic system. It synthesises and secretes certain neurohormones which in turn stimulate or inhibit the secretion of pituitary hormones. It controls other activities also like sleep, hunger, body temperature, etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Inhibin is composed of
questions.solution: Inhibins are dimeric glycoproteins composed of an $\alpha$-subunit and either a $\beta_{\mathrm{A}}$ (inhibin A) or a $\beta_{\mathrm{B}}$ subunit (inhibin B). They are mainly produced in gonads and provide negative regulation of FSH secretion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following pituitary hormones works indirectly?
questions.solution: Among the given hormones, TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone) secreted by anterior lobe of pituitary gland, works indirectly. This hormone controls the growth and activity of thyroid gland. It influences the uptake of iodine, the synthesis of the hormones; thyroxine and tri-iodothyronine by the thyroid gland. Rest of the hormones, i.e. MSH (Melanocyte Stimulating Hormone), GH (Growth Hormone) and oxytocin work directly on their target organ. They do not stimulate any other gland.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is incorrect about inhibin?
questions.solution: Statement (1) is incorrect about inhibin. It is a glycoprotein, not lipoprotein. In females, it is secreted by the corpus luteum while in males it is secreted by Sertoli cells. Inhibin inhibits FSH production from the anterior lobe of pituitary gland. Its molecular weight is $10-30 \mathrm{k}$ Dalton.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the function of Kupffer's cells?
questions.solution: The main function of Kupffer's cells is phagocytosis. They are specialised macrophages located in the liver, lining the walls of the sinusoids. Kupffer's cell activation is responsible for early ethanol induced liver injury, common in chronic alcoholics.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Peyer's patches are present in
questions.solution: eum. They are organised lymphoid follicles. They form an important part of the immune system by monitoring intestinal bacteria populations. They prevent the growth of pathogenic bacteria in the intestine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Daily requirement of vitamin-A for adult women is
questions.solution: The recommended daily amount of vitamin-A for adult women is 700 micrograms. Vitamin-A is a nutrient important for good vision, growth, cell division, reproduction and immunity. It is found in spinach, dairy products, etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Brunner's gland is located in
questions.solution: The Brunner's glands are located in duodenum only. They secrete a little enzyme and mucus. The mucus protects the duodenal wall from getting digested. The Brunner's glands open into the crypts of Lieberkuhn.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Where is sacculus rotandus located?
questions.solution: Sacculus rotundus is located between ileum and caecum. The junction of ileum and large intestine is seen in the form of an orifice called ileocolic or ostium ileocaecal valve. This portion is well- developed in rabbit in the form of swollen portion called sacculus rotandus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Purkinje's fibres are found in
questions.solution: rt. These are the part of impulse conducting network of the heart. They rapidly transmit impulses from the atrioventricular node to the ventricles.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Rouleaux formation is related to which of the cell/tissue?
questions.solution: Rouleaux formation is related to RBCs. In resting and slow flowing blood, the RBCs aggregate to form rouleaux, i.e. they are piled up on the top of each other. Fibrinogen favours rouleaux formation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is/are is the function(s) of calcium?
questions.solution:
Calcium performs all the given functions, i.e. blood clotting, muscular contraction and nerve conduction. $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ ions are helpful in the formation of pro-thrombinase which catalyses breakdown of prothrombin into thrombin and small peptide fragments.
Thrombin is important for the clotting of blood. Calcium plays a key regulatory role in muscle contraction. It helps in exposing the active sites on the F-actin molecules for myosin cross-bridges. Calcium ions help in the transmission of nerve impulse at a chemical synapse.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Loss of water from body occurs by all of the following except
questions.solution: The loss of water from body occurs by lungs, kidney and skin. Muscles do not lose water. Skin loses water in the form of sweat. Kidneys loose water in the form of urine. From lungs, during respiration some water is lost.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one is present in the urine of pregnant woman?
questions.solution: hCG (human Chorionic Gonadotropin) is present in the urine of pregnant woman. It is secreted by placenta. It stimulates the corpus luteum that continues to secrete progesterone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The correct sequence is
questions.solution:
ygote \rightarrow  Cleavage \rightarrow  Morula \rightarrow  Blastula \rightarrow  Gastrula.
At about $30-36 \mathrm{hrs}$ after fertilisation, the zygote divides into smaller cells by a process called cleavage. It is division of cells. It results in a solid ball of cells, called morula. It is a 16 -celled stage. It forms blastula which is a 64 -celled stage. It contains a fluid-filled cavity called blastocoel. It ultimately leads to gastrula stage. It is a multilayered structure which is followed by organogenesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is acrosomal reaction?
options: Contact of acrosome and nucleus of egg
questions.solution: Acrosomal reaction is digestion of zona pellucida. This involves the progressive fusion of the acrosomal membrane with the plasma membrane of the sperm. It creates pores through which the acrosomal enzymes can be released by exocytosis. These enzymes include a protein digesting enzyme, corona penetrating enzyme, zona lysin (acrosin) and hyaluronidase. These enzymes allow the sperm to digest a path through the zona pellucida to the oocyte.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Fimbriae are associated with which organ?
questions.solution: Fimbriae are associated with Fallopian tubes. Each Fallopian tube is about $10-12 \mathrm{~cm}$ long and consists of four parts viz., infundibulum, ampulla, isthmus and the uterine part. Fimbriae are finger-like projections found on the ends of infundibulum. They help in the collection of ovum after ovulation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Formation of corpus luteum is induced by
questions.solution: The formation of corpus luteum is induced by LH (Luteinising Hormone).The LH causes ovulation and remaining cells of the ovarian follicle develop corpus luteum. It secretes large amount of progesterone which is essential for the maintenance of uterine endometrium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is ribotide?
questions.solution: Ribotide is a nucleotide containing ribose as its pentose component. It is considered a molecular precursor of nucleic acids. In living organisms, the most common bases for ribotides are adenine, guanine, cytosine or uracil. Therefore, option (1), i.e. ribose + uracil + phosphate is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Linker-DNA is attached to
questions.solution: \mathrm{H}_1$ histone length. Linker DNA connects two adjacent nucleosomes. Its length is varied (about $145 Å$ with 70 bp). Nucleosome and linker DNA together constitute chromatosome. Chromatosome contains a histone octamer and DNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: To which of the following, repressor protein is attached?
questions.solution: Repressor protein is attached to operator gene. It is a regulatory protein synthesised by regulator gene. Repressor is meant for blocking the operator gene so that the structural genes are unable to form mRNAs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following mRNA can be transcripted as
questions.solution: Among the given options, only first one can be transcripted because it possesses an initiation codon-AUG which codes for methionine. Rest of the mRNA sequences start with termination codons, i.e. UAA (Ochre), UAG (Amber) and UGA (Opal). Therefore, these cannot be transcripted.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which is present at $5^{\prime}$ end of eukaryotic mRNA?
questions.solution: At the 5' end of eukaryotic mRNA, 7 mG (7-methyl guanosine) is present. In eukaryotes, primary transcript is often larger than the functional RNAs. Therefore, post-transcription processing is required to convert primary transcript of all types of RNAs into functional RNAs. It is of four types; cleavage, splicing, terminal additional and nucleotide modification. The terminal additions include capping and tailing. In capping, 7 mG is added to $5^{\prime}$ end of mRNA. In tailing, polyadenylation occurs which is addition of poly (A) tail to $3^{\prime}$ end of mRNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Non-disjunction in meiosis results in
questions.solution: somy, i.e. the presence of an extra chromosome. Such individuals have 47 chromosomes instead of 46 . Some examples of such abnormalities include Down's syndrome (21-trisomy), Patau's syndrome (13-trisomy) and Edward's syndrome (18-trisomy).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: AB blood group shows
questions.solution: In humans, AB blood group shows codominance. Here, allele $\mathrm{I}^{\mathrm{A}}$ for A-type blood is codominant with allele $\mathrm{I}^{\mathrm{B}}$ for B-type blood. In heterozygotes, $\mathrm{I}^{\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{I}^{\mathrm{B}}$ expresses the characteristics of both A and B antigens, i.e. $\mathrm{I}^{\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{I}^{\mathrm{B}}$ possess RBCs that carry both A and B antigens at their surface.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which trait is shown by given pedigree analysis?
questions.solution: The given pedigree analysis is showing autosomal dominant trait. If such a trait is present in pedigree, it seldom skips a generation. An autosomal recessive trait may skip a generation. A sex-linked dominant trait is more common in females while a sex-linked recessive trait is more common in males.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: $\mathrm{XYY} \rightarrow$ composition
questions.solution: The individuals having XYY chromosomes are known as super males. They have an additional Y chromosome. They suffer from poly Y male syndrome. These individuals are characterised by abnormal height, mental retardation, antisocial and criminal bent of mind.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one is an anti-allergic antibody?
questions.solution: IgE is an anti-allergic antibody. It plays a pivotal role in response to allergens such as anaphylactic drugs, bee stings, etc. They are synthesised by plasma cells. It is found in only mammals.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is involved in passive immunity?
questions.solution: IgA antibody is involved in passive immunity. This type of immunity is produced by a donor other than the infected person or an animal. It is short lived. Human colostrum (Mother's first milk) is rich in IgA antibodies. It provides natural passive immunity to the infant till the age of three months.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: Which one is used in tissue culture?
questions.solution: Explant is used in plant tissue culture. It is an excised plant part which has the potential to give rise to whole new plant. The plants obtained through this technique are morphologically and genetically similar to each other and to their parent plant.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Gene transfer is present in
questions.solution: olistics. This technique involves firing of microscopic gold particles coated with the foreign DNA at the cells using a compressed air gun. It is designed to overcome the problem of strong cell wall in plant tissues. These particles can penetrate the cell wall, the cell and the nuclear membrane to deliver the DNA to the nucleus.
